chapters.message: The payment share of 2024 does not exceed 2023; the payment story is not yet the largest the window has seen. It sits +1.1 pts above 2006 (interval +1.0 pts to +1.3 pts), so the 2006 peak is passed, and the window's own peak is 2023.
chapters.title: Affordable is a decision

chapters.message: The rate part of the payment overtook the price part in 2023Q3. The rate shock froze turnover where owners had the most to lose: 0.06 fewer purchases per 100 owner households per point of lock in (interval -0.08 to -0.03), and the placebo on the years before the shock sits at 0.00 with an interval that includes zero.
chapters.title: The rate shock and the lock in

chapters.message: The median renter is burdened in 51% of metros in 2024, so the median hides nothing; the problem is the whole distribution, with 26.5% of renters paying half or more (interval 25.7% to 27.2%). The national series moved and stayed moved in 2009, 2015, 2021.
chapters.title: The rent burden is a distribution problem

chapters.message: Where builders kept pace, prices rose less: 8.0% less price growth over 5 years per extra permit per hundred households (interval -14.3% to -1.7%); without the demand control the estimate is -0.4%. The estimate does not survive the window test: over 3 years 0.0%, 7 years +1.1% per window, with intervals that include zero, so this is a 5 year statement and the interior table says so.
chapters.title: Where builders kept pace, prices rose less

chapters.message: The ranking changes when you hold constant what people earn there: 17 of the 20 largest metros move beyond their intervals. Less affordable than their price says: Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater from 106 to 90; Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach from 33 to 22; Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim from 7 to 2. More affordable: St. Louis from 223 to 307; Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington from 114 to 195; Washington-Arlington-Alexandria from 25 to 102.
chapters.title: The fair ranking

chapters.message: The buyer is richer than in 2019 by +0.15 of the local median income (interval +0.12 to +0.19) and, against the claim, slightly younger: the under 35 share rose +1.2 pts (interval +0.1 pts to +2.3 pts) by 2025. The ratio moved most in Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim +0.44; Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach +0.37; New York-Newark-Jersey City +0.30.
chapters.title: Who still buys

chapters.message: The metros that gained people were already lagging before the pandemic: the placebo on the years before it is -0.8% (interval -1.4% to -0.2%), so the headline of +1.5% price growth over the window per person gained per hundred residents beyond the pre pandemic pace is a lower bound on what the migration itself did.
chapters.title: The migration shock

chapters.message: Buying beats renting only after 10.0 years in the typical metro (interval 1.0 years to beyond 30 years), and one point of rate moves the breakeven by +4.5 years. Longest to break even among the largest metros: Boston-Cambridge-Newton 21 years; Chicago-Naperville-Elgin 20 years; San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont 18 years.
chapters.title: The reader decision
